correctness.rationale: Every admissible strictly convex parallel-opposite hexagon admits the positive affine normal form. Six exact support inequalities are necessary and sufficient for containment after translation. Their interval intersection yields exactly λS≥S+t and λ(S+t)≥S. At equality three active facets force a unique center. The strict range follows from positivity, and every value in [1,2) is explicitly constructed. The packaged standard-library checker independently enumerates 375 exact rational LP solutions plus 3424 rational support/convexity cases; finite tests supplement rather than replace the universal proof.

originality.rationale: The full 2026 CPPOS primary and original 2013 CPPOS work concern affine equidistants, area bounds, and symmetry sets, not the exact homothetic containment minimum or its uniquely optimizing point. The universal one-ratio reduction for arbitrary noncentrally symmetric six-edge CPPOS is not implied by their theorems. Direct semantic searches for the same ratio, facet-normal dual and center rigidity returned results about different invariants. The classical Grünbaum paper optimizes a distinct area-partition functional. Older unindexed coverage and one 2026 abstract-only manuscript remain explicit risks.

value.rationale: A complete affine-invariant classification of the Minkowski asymmetry, optimizing center, and sharp range for the first genuinely noncentrally symmetric family of convex polygons with paired opposite side directions. Four positive shape parameters collapse to one scalar balance and the critical point is always unique. This answers a natural geometric-symmetry invariant not addressed by 2026 CPPOS area/Wigner-caustic results, rather than an arbitrary finite or perturbative subcase.
